content:
maya: Quick design review please — prototype for compact catalog rows + new pin affordance. link: https://figma.redwood/proto/compact-pin

sam: catching up — what's the main user need we're solving here?

maya: two things: 1) make pinning a version less visually heavy when people browse compare tables; 2) let users see pinned version context without expanding full row. idea: a micro chip on the row + small chevron to expand details.

alex: looks promising. question: if chip sits inline with performance badges does it collapse on small widths?

maya: yes — responsive: chip moves to right-most column and collapses into an overflow menu at < 640px.

jin: a11y flag: the chip needs a clear accessible name and keyboard target. propose aria-label: `Pin version 2.1 for model X` and role=button. also ensure focus ring visible in dark theme.

rachel: microcopy suggestion: instead of `Pinned` use `Pinned version` on hover, and tooltip copy: `Pinned version: 2.1 — used for compare and rollouts`. shorter inline label stays `Pinned`.

cory: engineering concern: if pinned variants are frequent we might blow up compare queries. can we lazy-fetch full pinned metadata only on expand?

maya: yes, plan is to surface minimal info (version id + perf badges) from main index and fetch config on expand.

oliver: from research sessions, users liked seeing a quick reason for a pin (e.g., "baseline for AB test"). maybe add a short reason line in the expanded panel (one-liner).

sam: product ask: make rollback action discoverable. If a user pins a version, they should be able to revert pin from same row without going to a modal. inline `Unpin` action?

alex: inline Unpin button okay but needs confirmation state. maybe `Unpin — Are you sure?` toast with undo.

jin: low-vision note: contrast for the chip background is borderline on our palette. suggest #1: stronger border; #2: a subtle background shift + maintain text contrast ratio 4.5:1.

rachel: copy for confirm: `Unpin version 2.1 — undone within 10s` (toast). keep language active voice.

maya: design tweak — make performance badges slightly smaller when chip present so row height doesn't jump. sample CSS: ```
.row .badge { --size: 12px; }
.row.pinned .badge { --size: 10px; }
```

cory: fine but watch pixel density on mobile. smaller badges might lose readability. plus more CSS states = more code paths.

alex: implementation plan: add `pinned` boolean to row item, render badge set compactly, keyboard focus target order: row -> pin -> expand -> actions. confirm?

jin: that focus order works. ensure aria-expanded on chevron and `aria-controls` to panel id. also add aria-live="polite" to the toast region for unpin confirmation.

oliver: quick note from testing: when multiple pins exist, users want a mini-legend explaining badges + pin state. could live as a help tooltip in the header.

sam: prioritization: MVP should include pin chip, inline unpin, and expanded reason. accessibility fixes and copy polish are next-sprint if too tight.

maya: thanks. I'll push updated frames with contrast adjustments and the `Pinned version` tooltip text. tagging @alex for fe pairing and @jin for a11y review when ready.

alex: I'll pair tomorrow AM. @ui-bot can we create a canary flag for `catalog_pin_ui_v2` so we can roll out to 10%?

ui-bot: Created feature flag `catalog_pin_ui_v2` set to 10% rollout for org `dev-team`. (deploys: none)

rachel: small nit: for screen readers, use `button` text: `Pin version menu` rather than generic `menu` to reduce ambiguity.

maya: good catch — updating. will post new prototype link when done. :thumbsup:
